title: Review Artifact

allOf.$comment: Under Review 1.1 an unrecognized disposition is a publication failure, so it cannot reach a downstream role as an otherwise valid handoff. That is what happened on the illusionist lineage: the term was read as unknown only when the Builder tried to compile against it, several artifacts later.

DEC-2026-0062: Review-contract 1.2 turns an approved_with_revision directive into an executable, row-local contract. The earlier spellings are deliberately not aliases: treating them as equivalent would convert historic authoring defects into unreviewed output changes. The top-level required_builder_revision block can describe publication and preservation, but cannot carry an executable row correction.

DEC-2026-0063: Integrator records only completed transactions or rejected bundles. A revision-required Review cannot route Integrator a pass/fail check with no record kind; the Reviewer must place passing check evidence in its approving successor. Both status fields are checked because queue derivation reads overall_disposition when present.

$comment: DEC-2026-0051: the only legal per-row Review dispositions are approved, approved_with_revision, rejected and architect_escalation. `approved_but_excluded_from_bundle` conflated two independent facts -- the Reviewer's judgment that a row is correct, and whether the row lands in an Approved edge component. The second is packaging, derived from the GUP's approved/pending/blocked components under DEC-2026-0047, and it is recorded as packaging evidence rather than as a fifth disposition. The check is opt-in on `review_contract_version: '1.1'` so that every Review published before this ruling stays valid immutable history.

review_contract_version.$comment: Opt-in marker for the DEC-2026-0051 vocabulary check. Absent means the Review predates it; a legacy Review is history, not a defect.

legalDisposition.$comment: ARTIFACT_LIFECYCLE section 4, unchanged since it was written.

rowDecision.$comment: Constrains only an object that actually carries a disposition. Reviews also use these keys for grouped summaries such as `approved_refs: [...]`, which state no per-row judgment and are left alone.

decisionCollection.$comment: Both published shapes are covered on purpose: a list of per-row objects, and a mapping whose values are those objects. Checking one shape and silently passing the other is how an invalid value survives a validator.

correctionDecisionCollection.$comment: The same list-or-mapping forms as decisionCollection, with the 1.2 correction payload rule on every actual disposition-bearing row.
